object_types.name: Person
object_types.definition: Anyone in the system, identified by a person ID.

source_references.excerpt: We track persons generally -- anyone in the system is a person with a person ID.

object_types.name: Employee
object_types.definition: A person who is employed; every employee is also a person, identified the same way.

source_references.excerpt: Employees are persons; every employee is also a person, identified the same way.

object_types.name: Manager
object_types.definition: An employee with extra responsibilities; every manager is also an employee, and through that, a person.

source_references.excerpt: A manager is an employee with extra responsibilities. Every manager is an employee, and through that, a person.

object_types.name: Department
object_types.definition: An organizational unit identified by a department code, with a unique name.

source_references.excerpt: Each department has a department code.
anyone in the system is a person with a person ID
Each department has a department code.

object_types.name: DepartmentName
object_types.definition: The name of a department, e.g. 'Payroll' or 'Field Operations'; no two departments share a name.

source_references.excerpt: Departments also each have a department name, like "Payroll" or "Field Operations", and no two share a name.
anyone in the system is a person with a person ID
Each department has a department code.
Departments also each have a department name, like "Payroll" or "Field Operations", and no two share a name.
Every employee works in exactly one department. Departments have many employees, but nobody is in two departments at once, and nobody is unassigned.
A manager manages at most one department. Some managers are between assignments and manage none.

ambiguities.description: Manager participation in managing a department is optional ('some managers manage none'), but is it also optional from the Department side -- can a Department exist without any manager, or must every Department eventually have exactly one manager? The transcript only states the manager side is optional.

source_references.excerpt: A manager manages at most one department. Some managers are between assignments and manage none.

ambiguities.description: Is the Department-to-Manager relationship one-to-one (each department managed by at most one manager) or could multiple managers be associated with a department in some other capacity? The transcript only explicitly constrains the Manager side ('at most one department'); the reverse cardinality is inferred, not stated.

source_references.excerpt: A manager manages at most one department.

ambiguities.description: The Employee-Department relationship ('works in') is described as a current, exactly-one-at-a-time assignment. It's unclear whether historical department assignments (transfers) need to be tracked, or whether this is current-state only.

source_references.excerpt: Every employee works in exactly one department.

ambiguities.description: Person, Employee, and Manager all share the same identification scheme (person_id) per the transcript, but it's worth confirming Manager doesn't have its own independent manager-specific identifier, since the transcript emphasizes 'through that, a person' without an explicit manager ID being ruled out.

source_references.excerpt: Every manager is an employee, and through that, a person.

ambiguities.description: DepartmentName is stated to be unique ('no two share a name'), raising the question of whether DepartmentName could serve as an alternate identifier for Department alongside DepartmentCode, and whether DepartmentCode is the preferred identifier or just one of two candidate keys.
